# nanovna-saver

**Sweep, chart and calibrate a NanoVNA from the computer**

- **Version recorded:** 0.7.3
- **Categories:** `antenna`, `electronics`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/NanoVNA-Saver/nanovna-saver>

## What it does

Connects to a NanoVNA or tinySA over USB serial, drives frequency sweeps, and displays S11/S21 as SWR, Smith chart, phase and magnitude plots -- with proper SOLT calibration, markers, and Touchstone export.

## Why you would want it

The NanoVNA's own screen is two inches across. This is how antenna measurements actually get read, compared and saved -- the de facto companion software for the most common antenna analyzer hardware in amateur radio.

## Before it will work

A NanoVNA-family device on USB and access to its serial port -- the `dialout` group. Calibration standards (the SOLT set that came with the device) for anything beyond rough looks.

## How it installs

- apt: `nanovna-saver`, `python3-pyside6.qtwidgets` — *on debian, parrot*
  - Debian 13 and Parrot 7 both offer 0.7.3-1.1 (measured 2026-09-06), the build that forgot its PySide6 dependency. `python3-pyside6.qtwidgets` is what 0.7.3-2 added to fix Debian bug #1112747 and it pulls QtCore and QtGui, the other two modules the program imports. From a clean Debian 13 VM the engine installed both and `NanoVNASaver` came up under Xvfb (2026-09-06), and the same on Parrot 7.3; without the second package it was a traceback. On a Debian release that ships the fixed package this block installs one package the archive would have installed anyway.
- apt: `nanovna-saver`
  - One `Architecture: all` package, so the arch selector this manifest used to carry is gone with the venv. Versions measured 2026-09-06 with `apt-cache policy` on the VM targets: Kali rolling 0.7.4~pre1-1, Ubuntu 26.04 0.7.4~pre1-1, Ubuntu 24.04 0.6.3-1, Pop!_OS 24.04 0.6.3-1 -- the 0.7.4 builds carry the PySide6 dependency and 0.6.3 is a PyQt6 program with its own. Installed through the engine on Ubuntu 24.04 and launched under Xvfb the same day. The 24.04 build is two minor versions behind; an operator who needs a feature from 0.7 on a 24.04 base is the case a venv block would be justified by, and nobody has asked yet.

## Known problems

Debian 13 and Parrot 7 ship 0.7.3-1.1, whose package forgot to depend on PySide6 (Debian bug #1112747): installed with plain apt it dies on `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'PySide6'`. This manifest installs `python3-pyside6.qtwidgets` beside it so the engine's install works; if you installed it by hand, that one package is the fix. The archive lags upstream: Ubuntu 24.04 carries 0.6.3 where Debian 13 has 0.7.3 and the rolling targets a 0.7.4 pre-release (measured 2026-09-06), so a device or firmware that upstream's changelog says was added recently may need the newer build. The command is `NanoVNASaver` and the package ships a menu entry. On Wayland, Qt may want QT_QPA_PLATFORM=xcb, the standing guidance.
